sanskrit: śaṃ na indrāgnī bhavatām avobhiḥ śaṃ na indrāvaruṇā rātahavyā | śam indrāsomā sa vitāya śaṃ yoḥ śaṃ na indrāpūṣaṇā vājasātau ||
english: May Indrāgnī be auspicious to us with their aids; may Indrāvaruṇa, to whom oblations are given, be auspicious to us; may Indrāsomā be auspicious for our well-being and bliss; may Indrāpūṣaṇa be auspicious to us in the winning of spoil.

sanskrit: śaṃ no bhagaḥ śam u naḥ śaṃso astu śaṃ naḥ purundhiḥ śam u santu rāyaḥ | śaṃ naḥ satyasya sūyamasya śaṃsaḥ śaṃ no aryamā purujāto astu ||
english: May Bhaga be auspicious to us, and may our praise be auspicious; may Puruṃdhī be auspicious to us and may riches be auspicious; may the laud of Truth, well-pressed, be auspicious to us; may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: śaṃ no dhātā śam u dhartā no astu śaṃ na urūcī bhavatu svadhābhiḥ | śaṃ rodasī bṛhatī śaṃ no adriḥ śaṃ no devānāṃ suhavāni santu ||
english: May Dhātṛ be auspicious to us, and Dhartṛ be auspicious to us; may the broad-stretching one be auspicious to us with her bounties; may the vast Rodasī be auspicious, may the stone be auspicious to us; may the invocations of the gods be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: śaṃ no agnir jyotiranīko astu śaṃ mitrāvaruṇāv aśvinā śam | śaṃ naḥ sukṛtāṃ sukṛtāni santu śaṃ na iṣiro abhi vātu vātaḥ ||
english: May Agni, whose face is light, be auspicious to us; may Mitrāvaruṇā be auspicious, and the Aśvins auspicious; may the good deeds of the righteous be auspicious to us; may the vigorous wind blow auspiciously upon us.

sanskrit: śaṃ no dyāvāpṛthivī pūrvahūtau śam antarikṣaṃ dṛśaye no astu | śaṃ na oṣadhīr vanino bhavantu śaṃ no rajasaḥ patir astu jiṣṇuḥ ||
english: May Dyāvāpṛthivī be auspicious to us at the first invocation; may the atmosphere be auspicious for our beholding; may the plants and the forest trees be auspicious to us; may the victorious Lord of the realm of dust be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: śaṃ na indro vasubhir devo astu śam ādityebhir varuṇaḥ suśaṃsaḥ | śaṃ no rudro rudrebhir jalāṣaḥ śaṃ nas tvaṣṭā gnābhir iha śṛṇotu ||
english: May Indra, the god together with the Vasus, be auspicious to us; may Varuṇa of excellent praise be auspicious with the Ādityas; may the refreshing Rudra be auspicious to us with the Rudras; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the goddesses hear us here with auspiciousness.

sanskrit: śaṃ naḥ somo bhavatu brahma śaṃ naḥ śaṃ no grāvāṇaḥ śam u santu yajñāḥ | śaṃ naḥ svarūṇāṃ mitayo bhavantu śaṃ naḥ prasvaḥ śam v astu vediḥ ||
english: May Soma be auspicious to us, may brahman be auspicious to us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious to us, may the sacrifices be auspicious; may the measured chants of the heavenly melodies be auspicious to us; may the pressing-ladle be auspicious to us, and the vedi be auspicious.

sanskrit: śaṃ naḥ sūrya urucakṣā ud etu śaṃ no bhavantu pradiśaś catasraḥ | śaṃ naḥ parvatā dhruvayo bhavantu śaṃ naḥ sindhavaḥ śam u santv āpaḥ ||
english: May Sūrya of wide sight rise auspiciously for us; may the four directions be auspicious to us; may the steadfast mountains be auspicious to us; may the rivers be auspicious to us, and may the waters be auspicious.

sanskrit: śaṃ no aditir bhavatu vratebhiḥ śaṃ no bhavantu marutaḥ svarkāḥ | śaṃ no viṣṇuḥ śam u pūṣā no astu śaṃ no bhavitraṃ śam v astu vāyuḥ ||
english: May Aditi be auspicious to us with her ordinances; may the Maruts, fond of the sun, be auspicious to us; may Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may our future be auspicious, and may Vāyu be auspicious.

sanskrit: śaṃ no devaḥ savitā trāyamānaḥ śaṃ no bhavantūṣaso vibhātīḥ | śaṃ naḥ parjanyo bhavatu prajābhyaḥ śaṃ naḥ kṣetrasya patir astu śambhuḥ ||
english: May the god Savitṛ, who protects, be auspicious to us; may the shining Dawns be auspicious to us; may Parjanya be auspicious to us for our offspring; may the Lord of the field, the beneficent one, be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: śaṃ naḥ satyasya patayo bhavantu śaṃ no arvantaḥ śam u santu gāvaḥ | śaṃ na ṛbhavaḥ sukṛtaḥ suhastāḥ śaṃ no bhavantu pitaro haveṣu ||
english: May the Lords of Truth be auspicious to us; may the horses be auspicious to us and the cattle be auspicious; may the Ṛbhus, of good deed and skillful hand, be auspicious to us; may the Pitṛs be auspicious to us at the oblations.

sanskrit: śaṃ no devā viśvadevā bhavantu śaṃ sarasvatī saha dhībhir astu | śam abhiṣācaḥ śam u rātiṣācaḥ śaṃ no divyāḥ pārthivāḥ śaṃ no apyāḥ ||
english: May the All-gods, the Viśvedevas, be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī be auspicious along with inspirations; may those that accompany the oblation and those that accompany the gift be auspicious; may the celestial, the terrestrial, and the aquatic be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: śaṃ no aja ekapād devo astu śam ahir budhnyaḥ śaṃ samudraḥ | śaṃ no apāṃ nāpat perur astu śaṃ naḥ pṛśnir bhavatu devagopāḥ ||
english: May Aja Ekapād, the god, be auspicious to us; may Ahir Budhnya be auspicious, and the ocean; may Apāṃ Napāt, the swift one, be auspicious to us; may Pṛśni, the god-guarded one, be auspicious to us.

sanskrit: ādityā rudrā vasavo juṣantām idaṃ brahma kriyamāṇaṃ navīyaḥ | śṛṇvantu no divyāḥ pārthivāso gojātā uta ye yajñiyāsaḥ ||
english: May the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus delight in this brahman-prayer being fashioned anew; may the celestial and terrestrial ones hear us, those born of cattle and those worthy of sacrifice.

sanskrit: ye devānām ṛtvijo yajñiyāso manor yajatrā amṛtā ṛtajñāḥ | te no rāsantām urugāyam adya yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā naḥ ||
english: Those divine priests who are worthy of sacrifice, who are adorable as Manu's, immortal and knowing the Ṛta — may they grant us wide renown today; do you all ever protect us with blessings.

sanskrit: tad astu mitrāvaruṇā tad agne śaṃ yor asmabhyam idam astu śastam | aśīmahi gātum uta pratiṣṭhāṃ namo dive bṛhate sādanāya ||
english: May that be so, O Mitrāvaruṇā, may that be so, O Agni; may this that is recited be auspicious and blissful for us; may we attain the path and firm footing; homage to the vast sky, to its abode.

sanskrit: agnāv agniś carati praviṣṭa ṛṣīṇāṃ putro adhirāja eṣaḥ | tasmai juhomi haviṣā ghṛtena mā devānāṃ yūyavad bhāgadheyam ||
english: Fire moves having entered into fire — this one is the supreme king, the son of the seers; to him I offer with an oblation of ghee; may the due portion of the gods not be withheld.

sanskrit: yukto vaha jātavedaḥ purastād agne viddhi kriyamāṇaṃ yathedam | tvaṃ bhiṣag bheṣajasyāpi kartā tvayā gām aśvaṃ puruṣaṃ sanema ||
english: Yoked, carry forward from the east, O Jātavedas; O Agni, know what is being performed here; you are the physician, the maker of the remedy; through you may we win cattle, horse, and man.

sanskrit: tathā tvam agne kṛṇu jātavedo 'nena vidvān haviṣā yaviṣṭha | piśāco asya yatamo jaghāsa yathā so asya paridhiṣ patāti ||
english: So do you act, O Agni Jātavedas, knowing through this oblation, O youngest one; whichever Piśāca has devoured this man, may it fall from his enclosure.

sanskrit: yo 'sya dideva yatamo jaghāsa yathā so asya paridhiṣ patāti | tathā tvam agne kṛṇu jātavedo viśvebhir devaiḥ saha saṃvidānaḥ ||
english: Whichever one has deceived and devoured this man, may it fall from his enclosure; so do you act, O Agni Jātavedas, in accord with all the gods.

sanskrit: akṣyau ni vidhya hṛdayaṃ ni vidhya jihvāṃ ni tṛndhi pra dataḥ śṛṇīhi | piśāco asya yatamo jaghāsa- -agne yaviṣṭha prati taṃ śṛṇīhi ||
english: Pierce out its eyes, pierce out its heart, cut out its tongue, crush its teeth; whichever Piśāca has devoured this man — O Agni, youngest one, smite that one in return.

sanskrit: yad asya hṛtaṃ vihṛtaṃ yat parābhṛtam ātmano jagdham uta yat piśācaiḥ | tad agne vidvān punar ā bhara tvaṃ śarīre prāṇam asum erayāsya ||
english: Whatever has been taken from him, dispersed, carried away, devoured from his own self, and whatever by Piśācas — that, O Agni, knowing it, do you bring back; stir up again the breath of life in his body.

sanskrit: apāṃ tvā pāne yatamo dadambha- -odane manthe yadi vota lehe | tad ātmanā prajayā piśācā vi yātayantām agado 'yam astu ||
english: Whichever Piśāca has injured you in the drinking of water, in porridge, in the stirred drink, or in what is licked — may the Piśācas pay penalty with their own selves and offspring; may this man be free of disease.

sanskrit: kṣīre tvā māṃse yatamo dadambha- -akṛṣṭapacye aśane dhānye yaḥ | tad ātmanā prajayā piśācā vi yātayantām agado 'yam astu ||
english: Whichever Piśāca has injured you in milk, in flesh, in food cooked without plowing, in grain — may the Piśācas pay penalty with their own selves and offspring; may this man be free of disease.

sanskrit: āme supakve śabale vipakve ya imaṃ piśāco aśane dadambha | tam indro vājī vajreṇa hantu bhinattu somaḥ śiro asya dhṛṣṇuḥ ||
english: Whichever Piśāca has injured this man in raw food, in well-cooked, in mixed, in half-cooked — may Indra the mighty slay it with his thunderbolt; may the bold Soma split open its head.

sanskrit: divā tvā naktaṃ yatamo dadambha kravyād yātuḥ śayane piśācaḥ | tad agne vidvān pra daha kṣiṇīhy apy enaṃ dhehi nirṛter upasthe ||
english: Whichever flesh-eating Piśāca sorcerer has injured you by day or by night while lying down — that, O Agni, knowing it, burn up and destroy; place it in the lap of Nirṛti.
